 (BY SHRI VINOD THAKUR, GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for order this day, th e cou  following:
 ORDER 01.

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 o f Cr.P.C., as he is implicated in connection with FIR/Crime No.145/2020 registered at Police Station Malhargarh,
District Mandsaur (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 409, 34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act and Section 6(1) of M.P. Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam.

sentences.text:
He is in custody since 27.12.2022.
02.
As per prosecution case, the main accused Fayaz Khan induced the complainant to invest in the Bit Coin trade alluring and assuring him huge profits.

He charged a total of Rs.62,000/- in three parts (24,000/- + 24,000/- + 14,000/-) under the pretext of making his ID to transact in the trade,
but later refused to return the same stating that the company, with whom he was dealing with has closed down their shutters and has disappeared.
Thereafter, an FIR was lodged against the main accused Fayaz Khan.
During Investigation, the present applicant is implicated in the case on the basis of memorandum statement of Fayaz Khan which was recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that total 31 crimes are registered against the present applicant including this present crime.
In all other crimes, he was granted bail except two cases.
The applicant is innocent and has not committed the offence and he has been falsely implicated in the case.
The main accused Fayaz Khan is granted bail by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 19.08.2020 in M.Cr.C. No.28244/2020.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
The trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, on this ground prayer is made to enlarged the applicant on bail.
04. Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and submits that the applicant has a criminal past.
Therefore, he is not entitled to get bail.
05. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

06. Considering the facts and circumstances coupled with the fact that final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

07. The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand) with two solvent sureties out of which one shall be local surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Certified copy as per rules.
